title: Shadow metering: tag usage records as baseline vs burst + reconciliation export
author: Cole Summers
body:
Title: Shadow metering: tag usage records as baseline vs burst + reconciliation export

Context
We’re piloting Dedicated “burst capacity” with initial terms of shadow billing. To support pricing validation + customer transparency + incident forensics, we need to (a) attribute usage as baseline vs burst at the usage-record level and (b) export a reconciliation report that finance/pricing can compare against routing/policy logs and pool-level burst usage.

This PR adds a first-pass attribution path in the metering pipeline that tags usage records with a burst classification and emits a daily reconciliation export. This is intentionally non-invoicing-impacting: all downstream invoice computation ignores the new field for now, and the export is written to a separate shadow location.

What changed (high level)
1) Usage record schema: add `capacity_class` = BASELINE | BURST | UNKNOWN (string enum in codegen; stored as a low-cardinality dimension, NOT a freeform tag).
2) Tagging rules: infer capacity_class from request context claims set by routing/data plane (see pr-8440 / pr-8466 dependencies) with defensive fallbacks.
3) Metering pipeline: persist capacity_class on usage records and propagate through aggregation jobs.
4) Reconciliation export: new daily job that writes per-tenant/per-region summaries of baseline vs burst usage (requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, billable_tokens) plus a “missing classification” counter.
5) Guardrails: sampling + cardinality controls (no model name, no prompt hash in export). Adds explicit alarms for UNKNOWN rate > threshold.

Why this approach
- We avoid retrofitting “burst” logic into invoice computation during pilot; we only enrich telemetry.
- We make reconciliation deterministic and auditable: capacity_class is derived from routing claims, not recomputed from fleet signals.
- We accept UNKNOWN when claims are missing; we’d rather under-attribute burst than accidentally mark baseline as burst.

Implementation details
- Request context -> metering: we use `x-rw-capacity-claim` (internal header) populated by the router when burst admission succeeded, and a signed internal claim in the request auth context for non-HTTP ingestion paths.
- Precedence order:
  (1) Explicit capacity claim from router context (BURST / BASELINE)
  (2) Dedicated tenant + burst_enabled + route_decision indicates burst_pool
  (3) Otherwise BASELINE for Dedicated
  (4) Otherwise UNKNOWN for non-Dedicated paths (should be rare; mainly internal batch jobs)
- Reconciliation export format (CSV gzip):
  - dt, tenant_id, tenant_name, region, capacity_class, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, billable_tokens, unknown_records
  - Written to: `s3://redwood-shadow-metering/burst-recon/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/...`
  - Also emits a JSON manifest for tooling compatibility.

Illustrative snippet
`CapacityClass classify(const UsageContext& ctx) {
  if (ctx.capacity_claim == "burst") return CapacityClass::BURST;
  if (ctx.capacity_claim == "baseline") return CapacityClass::BASELINE;
  if (!ctx.is_dedicated_tenant) return CapacityClass::UNKNOWN;
  if (ctx.route_decision.pool_type == PoolType::BURST) return CapacityClass::BURST;
  return CapacityClass::BASELINE;
}`

Operational notes
- Unknown classification rate should be ~0% for Dedicated traffic once routing rollout is complete. During staged rollout we expect some unknowns; we include `unknown_records` in the export to quantify this.
- If we see UNKNOWN spikes during an incident, SRE can correlate with router header propagation issues (runbook follow-up in ENG-4827).

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - capacity_class precedence ordering
  - Dedicated baseline defaulting
  - Unknown handling when claims missing
- Integration tests:
  - e2e metering record contains capacity_class for simulated Dedicated burst-admitted request
  - aggregation job keeps capacity_class split stable
- Load test sanity: replayed 30m of pilot traffic in staging; CPU impact of tagging was within noise (<1%).

Rollout
- Feature gated by `metering.capacity_classification_enabled` (default off).
- Staging: enable for one test tenant + us-east-1.
- Pilot: enable for design partners only, then expand once UNKNOWN rate is stable.

Follow-ups
- Add join keys between export rows and routing admission logs to support deeper forensics (not in scope here; will do after we validate first export consumers).
- Add a lightweight internal dashboard panel for baseline vs burst split per tenant once data is flowing (Telemetry/SRE).

Review notes / discussion
- Nadia requested we never include model_id in the export due to cardinality + external sharing risk; removed in commit 7.
- Logan requested explicit metric for UNKNOWN rate and a hard alert during pilot; added `metering_capacity_class_unknown_ratio` + alert stub.
- Jordan requested deterministic behavior when both header and claim present but disagree; we now prefer signed claim and emit a counter `capacity_claim_mismatch_total`.

Checklist
- [x] Schema change backwards compatible
- [x] No invoice computation changes
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Added docs note in metering README
- [x] Feature flag default off

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- metering-integration: pass
- lint: pass
- data-jobs-compile: pass

Conversation excerpts
- Nadia Rahman (review): “Can we guarantee this doesn’t change invoicing? Also, please don’t add any high-card dimensions to the export.”
- Cole Summers (author): “Confirmed invoicing ignores capacity_class; export is separate bucket/prefix + new flag. Removed model_id and prompt hash; only tenant/region/capacity_class.”
- Logan Wright (review): “We need a counter for mismatched claims. This will bite us during rollout.”
- Cole Summers (author): “Added `capacity_claim_mismatch_total` and prefer signed claim; header mismatch increments counter.”
- Sean Gallagher (review): “Operationally I want UNKNOWN ratio paged only during pilot; make sure threshold is gated.”
- Cole Summers (author): “Alert rule is stubbed behind the same pilot flag; default disabled.”

Merge
Squash merged to main after approvals from Nadia + Logan + Jordan + Sean. Release note: none (internal-only shadow metering).
